attacks.target: R2: does the contract goalpost catch a README that was correct yesterday and stale today - the apex_probes.py June defect class (truth surface correct at write time, stale when the reference moves)?
evidence: YES - same shape as apex_probes June defect. The README is a truth surface pinned at write time; the REFERENCE (git release tags) moves when a release is published. The gate re-derives the newest tag on every run and compares: a README that was green yesterday (all arms ok at 5.52.0) flips RED the day tag v5.53.0 appears. Reproduced in the throwaway repo as CASE B above - the previous-green README went red on BOTH tag_not_ahead_of_banner and tag_claim_current with zero local edits to the README; only the tag set changed.

Release-window asymmetry is deliberate and does not false-red a correct workflow: banner/VERSION ahead of newest tag stays green (unit test test_green_in_release_window_face_ahead_of_tag + live basis = max(newest tag, VERSION) in tag_claim_current, so a dev bump between releases stays green indefinitely). The ONLY reds are real drift: tag outrunning the face, stale/missing banner, banner != VERSION, stale or impossible 'is latest' claim.

Unmeasurable is never a verdict: no git / no tags -> 'nothing to compare' checks stay green with a stated reason (test_no_tags_is_nothing_to_compare_never_red); an absent claim is allowed (test_absent_tags_claim_is_allowed). Same unmeasured!=wrong posture as the APEX arm.

The June class is also caught by the APEX arm of the same verifier (apex_probes stamp vs freshest apex_truth artifact) - that arm stays green today because stamp 22.0.400 == freshest artifact 22.0.400 (verified).
